name: Sellrain
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Sellraintal valley featuring a stunning Baroque parish church and breathtaking hikes in the Naturpark.
beschreibung:
Overview

Sellrain is situated at an elevation of 908 meters in the Sellraintal valley (Melachtal) within the Northern Stubai Alps in the Innsbruck-Land district, approximately 18 kilometers southwest of Innsbruck. Home to around 1,350 residents, the municipality stretches from the valley floor along the rushing Melach stream, through the pristine Fotschertal side valley, up to rugged Alpine summits exceeding 2,800 meters. Together with its neighboring hamlets of Gries and St. Sigmund, Sellrain belongs to the exclusive international Mountaineering Villages (Bergsteigerdörfer) initiative of the Alpine Convention. Free from mass ski developments, Sellrain embodies gentle alpinism, untouched landscapes, world-class ski mountaineering, and authentic Tyrolean mountain hospitality.

History

Human presence in the valley dates back to the Stone Age: at the Ullafelsen rock in the Fotschertal, archaeologists uncovered a 10,000-year-old Mesolithic hunting camp, considered one of the Eastern Alps' most important prehistoric sites. Sellrain was first formally documented in 1271 (and in 1289 under Count Meinhard II) under the pre-Roman name Selrain. Monasteries such as Wilten and Frauenchiemsee established dairy farms (Schwaighöfe) here during the High Middle Ages, alongside modest iron and silver mining. The architectural marvel of the area is the pilgrimage church of Saint Quirinus: perched like an eagle's nest on a precipitous rocky crag at 1,243 meters, this sanctuary was first recorded in 1391 and preserves a magnificent late Gothic winged altarpiece crafted around 1510/1515. Pilgrims sought its healing waters for centuries. The Baroque parish church of Saint Anne was constructed between 1701 and 1705.

Getting there

Sellrain enjoys reliable access throughout the year. Motorists exit the A12 Inntal motorway at Zirl-Ost/Kematen, following the Sellraintal state road L13 for just eight kilometers (about ten minutes' drive) straight to the village center. A dramatic mountain road also connects from the west via the Kühtai pass (L11). Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station or the regional stop in Kematen in Tirol. VVT regional bus line 4166 runs frequent services from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof directly through Kematen to Sellrain and onward to Gries and Kühtai.

Tips

Hike up the spiritual path to the clifftop pilgrimage sanctuary of Saint Quirinus for dramatic aerial views of the valley and to admire its carved Gothic altarpiece. In both summer and winter, explore the tranquil, car-free Fotschertal valley, known for idyllic hiking paths, natural tobogganing runs, and classic ski touring routes. Experienced mountaineers can base themselves at the Potsdamer Hütte (2,012 m) to ascend the Roter Kogel (2,832 m) for breathtaking vistas stretching from the Kalkkögel to the Stubai glaciers. Sellrain also serves as a trailhead for the Austrian Alpine Club’s challenging seven-day Sellrain Mountain Hut Trek.
